provider_specific_fields.message: Free tier monthly allowance exhausted. Upgrade to Builder ($29/mo) for $20 of included usage + BYOK.

/v1/messages.method: from-code (rendered in fixture env with the real Flux renderer)
/v1/messages.headers_note: content-type and content-length are from the real renderer. The security headers seen on every live chat capture (x-frame-options, content-security-policy, x-content-type-options) are app-wide and expected here too, but these routes were NOT live-captured (staging does not mount the Flux /v1/messages and /v1/responses handlers). x-request-id is echoed on /v1/messages only when the client sent one.

notes: Raised by the Flux rate limiter (src/rate_limits.py), which runs BEFORE forge_hook stamps the subscription tier. On /v1/chat/completions the forge failure hook (src/gateway.py:26070-26088) therefore sees tier='free' for EVERY key, finds 'exceeded' in str(exc) ('rate_limit_exceeded'), and rewrites the 429 into this 402 free_tier_exhausted. The original 429 body survives only on /v1/messages (message only) and /v1/responses (full dict, incl. error.state). No Retry-After / reset header on any endpoint. The per-tier RPM burst limit (free 60, payg 600, builder 1000, scale 10000, enterprise 50000) is reported as a 402 on chat; on /v1/messages the message is the fallback 'upstream error (status 429)' because the body has no message field. retry_after:60 exists only inside the /v1/responses body.
